description:
Advances: ancora.scaffold

Wave 1 of ancora-gg8 (C1 in the investigation record; findings-C and the architecture decision are comments there). The command verification kind stays retired per ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state. The blessed successor for forbidden-text tripwires is the tagged ExUnit source-scan test — three Atlas sessions hand-derived ~100-line scanners in one day, and a hand-rolled scanner without the vacuity guard is a silent green. The reference implementation is atlas test/atlas/graph/access_scoping_logs_test.exs (commit c84d727ff).

Deliverable:
1. `Ancora.SourceScan` — a deliberately tiny test-support module (~80 lines, lib/ancora/source_scan.ex): declarative scan config (dirs/globs, forbidden tokens or regexes, allowlist of paths), whole-token matching by default (negative lookaround, so a binding is not matched inside a longer identifier or string), and a baked-in vacuity guard — a scan whose file set is empty raises/fails rather than passing. Pure File.read! of the working tree; no shell, no ports; it runs in the CONSUMER's test suite, never in an ancora task, so no_execution_no_state is untouched. Consumers tag the wrapping test with `@tag spec:` as usual.
2. docs/migration.md gains a "command gates" section: the successor recipe with a copyable template using Ancora.SourceScan, the two things people get wrong called out (vacuity guard, whole-token matching), and a migration-checklist line noting that migration-driven load shifts are a real cost (retagged suites and added compile can tip latent consumer flakes — the atlas-5wi lesson).
3. New subject .spec/specs/ancora.source_scan.spec.md authored in this diff (spec language below), with tagged tests anchoring it in the same diff.

Spec delta (land in this same diff):
- New subject `ancora.source_scan` (kind: module, status: active, decisions: ancora.decision.field_friction_response, ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state). Requirements (all must):
  - source_scan.declarative_config: scan/1 takes dirs-or-globs, tokens (strings or regexes), and an allowlist; returns violations as {file, line, token} tuples.
  - source_scan.vacuity_guard: a scan resolving to zero files shall fail loudly, never pass silently.
  - source_scan.whole_token_matching: a plain-string token shall match only as a whole token; substring hits inside longer identifiers shall not count. Regex tokens are used verbatim.
  - source_scan.no_execution: the module shall do no process spawning, no shell, no Port — file reads only (covered by the existing forbidden-spawner static test's scope).
  One Given/When/Then per must; verification kind tagged_tests covering all four.
- Edit the `ancora.scaffold.migration_doc` statement: append "and shall document the command-gate successor: the tagged ExUnit source-scan pattern with `Ancora.SourceScan`, including the vacuity guard and whole-token matching."

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests for all four source_scan requirements (fixture dirs with planted violations, an empty-glob vacuity case, a substring non-match case); scaffold/migration doc test updated for the new section.
- Behaviors to demonstrate: each new scenario; the migration.md template compiles as a real test when copied into a fixture project.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale plus targeted files, and mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: before IMPLEMENTED, full mix test plus mix spec.check --base <stage-base>, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base <stage-base> and targeted/--stale selections only; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Fixture/sandbox hygiene: async-safe fixtures, no cross-test leakage
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test
- Call-site Integration: Ancora.SourceScan's production callers are consumer test suites; the proving path here is ancora's own tagged tests exercising the public scan/1 API exactly as the migration.md template shows (the template and the tests must stay in lockstep).

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/gate.ex
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- lib/ancora/finding.ex
- lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex

Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/source_scan.ex (new)
- docs/migration.md
- test/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.source_scan.spec.md (new, authored per the spec language above)
- .spec/specs/ancora.scaffold.spec.md (the migration_doc statement edit above, plus acknowledgment edits for this stage's own changes only)
- .spec/decisions/ancora.decision.field_friction_response.md (exactly one change: add `- ancora.source_scan` to affects:; orchestrator ruling 2026-09-03T23:00Z)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No verification-kind or schema changes — this is a test-support module plus docs, not gate vocabulary
- No declarative forbidden-pattern built-in in the gate (declined on the epic)
- No scanning smarts beyond whole-token/regex (AST-aware matching stays in consumer-written scanners when they need it)
- Updates to the spec-led-development / spec-led-bootstrap skills live outside this repo and are tracked on the epic, not here

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

TEST_CRITIC: DEFECTS
Session: e92f6de6-94f7-4814-8140-19f3f3007d0a
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-remembers/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/e92f6de6-94f7-4814-8140-19f3f3007d0a.jsonl

Reviewed test/ancora/source_scan_test.exs and test/ancora/scaffold/docs_test.exs at 72ac7f7 against ancora.source_scan.spec.md, the ancora.scaffold.migration_doc edit, and the ticket contract. Both files pass (7 tests, 0 failures). Fixture hygiene is sound: every fixture test uses @tag :tmp_dir, modules are async: true, expected paths derive from the per-test dir, and the vacuity test correctly proves the guard fires AFTER the allowlist empties a non-empty set (3-arity assert_raise with the exact message). The template-fixture test in docs_test.exs is a real lockstep check: renaming a scan/1 option breaks the copied template and the subprocess exits non-zero.

I ran five hand mutations of lib/ancora/source_scan.ex against a scratch copy of the tagged tests. All five stayed green. Three are defects.

DEFECT 1 — test/ancora/source_scan_test.exs:20-27 (declarative_config): glob expansion is never load-bearing.
The glob Path.join(nested, "*.ex") only names files the directory entry Path.join(root, "lib") already yields. Mutation: replace the non-directory branch of resolve_path/1 with Enum.filter([path], &File.regular?/1) (no Path.wildcard). Result: 4 tests, 0 failures. docs_test.exs's fixture also passes because lib/ supplies files so the vacuity guard never fires.
Failure let through: a consumer following the migration template with ["lib", "config/*.exs"] silently never scans config/. Silent green, the exact class this ticket exists to kill.
Fix: plant a violation in a file reachable ONLY through the glob (e.g. root/config/runtime.exs via Path.join(root, "config/*.exs")) and expect it in the result.

DEFECT 2 — test/ancora/source_scan_test.exs:51-61 (whole_token_matching): only the leading underscore boundary is proven.
Mutation A: drop the trailing (?![[:alnum:]_]) lookahead. Result: green. Failure let through: token "cmd" matches "cmdline = 1" (false positive; loud but wrong, and the requirement statement "shall not match inside a longer identifier" is half-unproven).
Mutation B: replace both lookarounds with \b...\b. Result: green. Failure let through: any plain-string token that starts or ends with a non-word char (":os.cmd", "@spec", "IO.inspect(") never matches at line start or before whitespace, because \b needs a word char on the other side. Silent green. The template dodges this by writing :os.cmd as a regex, which hides the gap rather than testing it.
Fix: add lines "cmdline = :safe" and ":os.cmd('x')" to the fixture; add tokens "cmd" (already) and ":os.cmd" as a plain string; expect the string ":os.cmd" hit and no "cmdline" hit.

DEFECT 3 — test/ancora/source_scan_test.exs:73-77 (no_execution) vs spec statement "shall not spawn processes".
The refutes cover System.cmd, System.shell, Port.open, :os.cmd. Mutation: change scan/1 to Task.async_stream(files, &violations(&1, tokens), timeout: :infinity). Result: green here AND green in test/ancora/static/forbidden_spawner_test.exs (its AST walk matches the same four call forms only). Failure let through: the requirement promises no process spawning; nothing anchors that half. Resolve one way or the other: either add refutes for "Task.", "spawn", "Process.spawn", ":erlang.open_port" (and ideally dogfood SourceScan.scan on its own source instead of a fourth hand-rolled scanner), or narrow the statement to shell/port calls, matching what the ticket actually scoped ("covered by the existing forbidden-spawner static test's scope"). As written, the test does prove something a scanner could violate (shelling out to grep/rg), so this is a statement/test mismatch, not a vacuous test.

Recommendations (not blocking):
- Regex.escape is unproven: dropping it stays green (token "System.cmd" then also matches "Systemxcmd"; a token containing "(" would raise at compile). A token with a metachar and a near-miss line would pin it.
- source_scan_test.exs:71 `scan(...) == []` on a safe file asserts nothing about execution; it only pads the no_execution test. Harmless.
- docs_test.exs:46-48 text-presence asserts on "vacuity guard" / "whole-token matching" are as strong as a doc requirement gets; fine.

Net: declarative_config and whole_token_matching each prove roughly half of what their requirement statements say, and the surviving halves are the silent-green ones. Two small fixture additions (one glob-only file, two extra source lines plus one plain-string token) close defects 1 and 2 in the same test file.

AUDIT: BOUNCE → implementer
Session: e92f6de6-94f7-4814-8140-19f3f3007d0a
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-remembers/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/e92f6de6-94f7-4814-8140-19f3f3007d0a.jsonl

Reasoning: Scope is clean (7 files, all Allowed, ADR moved exactly one affects: line, no trailer) and the vacuity_guard test at test/ancora/source_scan_test.exs:31 plus the fixture-project lockstep test at test/ancora/scaffold/docs_test.exs:53 are load-bearing. But two of the four must requirements survive the mutations their statements forbid, so the tagged tests are not load-bearing for them. (1) declarative_config, source_scan_test.exs:20-27: the glob entry Path.join(nested, "*.ex") only yields files the directory entry Path.join(root, "lib") already expands via "**/*", and Enum.uniq collapses them; replacing the non-directory branch of resolve_path/1 with Enum.filter([path], &File.regular?/1) leaves every test in the file and the docs fixture green (config/*.exs contributes nothing there because lib/ keeps the file set non-empty). The verifier's "Would fail if scan/1 dropped ... the glob branch" claim is false. (2) whole_token_matching, source_scan_test.exs:51-61: the fixture "system_cmd = :safe" only exercises the leading lookbehind. Dropping the trailing (?![[:alnum:]_]) stays green, and swapping both lookarounds for \b stays green, even though \b silently never matches a plain-string token that begins or ends with a non-word char such as ":os.cmd" at line start. The ticket promised negative lookaround specifically; the test cannot tell it from \b. (3) no_execution: the spec statement says "shall not spawn processes" but source_scan_test.exs:73-77 refutes only System.cmd/System.shell/Port.open/:os.cmd, and test/ancora/static/forbidden_spawner_test.exs:36-60 walks the same four call forms, so a Task.async_stream or spawn in scan/1 passes both. The verifier recorded this as a Note; it is a must statement with an unanchored half.

Bounce reason: In test/ancora/source_scan_test.exs, make all three halves falsifiable. For declarative_config: add a file reachable only through a glob, e.g. write Path.join(root, "config/runtime.exs") containing System.cmd("x", []), pass Path.join(root, "config/*.exs") in dirs_or_globs (root/config must not also be listed as a directory), and expect {that_file, 1, "System.cmd"} in the sorted result. For whole_token_matching: extend the fixture to "system_cmd = :safe\ncmdline = :safe\n:os.cmd('x')\ncmd = :violation\n", add the plain string ":os.cmd" to tokens, and expect a ":os.cmd" string hit on its line, "cmd" only on the standalone line, and no "cmdline" hit; this kills both the dropped-lookahead and the \b substitutions. For no_execution: add refutes on the module source for "spawn", "Task.", "Process.", and ":erlang.open_port" using the same string-concatenation spelling as the existing refutes (the current module text contains none of them), so the statement "shall not spawn processes" has a test that fails on a Task.async_stream rewrite. Keep the docs/migration.md template unchanged unless the scan/1 keys change. Re-run the change-scoped final tier including mix spec.check --base 9373ff49ea0ce4bbe0069f4961094eee28fc0e81 and post a fresh IMPLEMENTED.
